speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Sustainability has always been part of Singapore’s development journey as we set out to create a clean, green, and liveable environment amid Singapore’s urban transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Through the Singapore Green Plan 2030, we renewed our commitment to put sustainability and resilience at the heart of our plans, to build a future-ready Singapore that continues to thrive in a world characterised by climate change, resource constraints, and growing uncertainties.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) will continue working with Singaporeans to steward a sustainable and resilient Singapore for future generations, in line with aspirations conveyed through the Forward Singapore exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Singapore Green Plan charts out concrete policies and actions for Singapore to decarbonise and achieve our net-zero ambition, and how the Government, businesses, community, and individuals can work together towards a greener future.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Government will enable this green transition by working with all segments of society to change our mindsets, habits, and behaviours, and supporting the creation of new sustainable business models and green jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will continue to advance effective international collaboration to support our decarbonisation efforts, such as in carbon markets, carbon capture usage and storage, a regional power grid, and renewable energy.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The public sector will reduce its electricity and water consumption and waste generation, and further enhance its green procurement policies.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Environmental stewardship means shifting away from a make-use-throw mindset, and embracing a circular economy and zero-waste culture.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Extended Producer Responsibility framework is an important enabler to encourage sustainable production upstream by requiring producers to be responsible for the collection and proper treatment of their products at end-of-life.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Manufacturers and importers will need to reframe their thinking, redesign their business processes and products, and consider environmental externalities throughout the life cycle of their products.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As a low-lying and densely built island nation, Singapore is vulnerable to rising sea levels and rising temperatures.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To adapt to increased flood risk, we will continue to enhance the effectiveness of our drainage network, and put in place multi-functional adaptation infrastructure for Singapore’s coastlines.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To preserve liveability amidst rising temperatures, the Government will expand our urban heat mitigation measures by increasing greenery and using cool paints.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This includes increasing the adoption of productive technologies and sustainable farming practices, making better use of land and sea spaces for agriculture and aquaculture, and encouraging demand for local produce.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Climate change will also raise the risk of vector-borne diseases like dengue and pose challenges to public health.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will invest in new capabilities to realise our sustainability ambitions and raise our national resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These efforts will be supported and sustained by a pipeline of local talent.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Singapore Green Plan is supported by a growing movement of individuals, community groups and businesses wishing to build a more sustainable and resilient Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Through Forward Singapore, the community, public, and private sectors have discussed how we can, as a society, foster a more sustainable way of life, and steward our environmental resources responsibly for future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Building a sustainable, resilient, and future-ready Singapore requires everyone to play a part.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We must change our mindsets, lifestyles and habits to build a more resilient and sustainable Singapore.
